title: kmac: where software selects the mode, and the squeeze status bit
conditions: Software configures KMAC (cSHAKE mode) before an operation, and later waits for the state to be readable.
Each setting is encoded as 1 if the register has the field (or bit) described and 0 if it does not.

requirements.text: If KMAC is enabled, the software should configure [`CMD.mode`](registers.md#cmd) to cSHAKE and the first six bytes of [`PREFIX`](registers.md#prefix) to `0x01204B4D4143` (bigendian).
If KMAC is enabled, the software should configure [`CFG_SHADOWED.mode`](registers.md#cfg_shadowed) to cSHAKE
requirements.note: Section "Software Initiated KMAC/SHA3 process". The same instruction as R1, with a different register.

requirements.text: appends proper ending bits with respect to the [`CFG_SHADOWED.mode`](registers.md#cfg_shadowed) value.
Or the software can poll the [`STATUS.squeeze`](registers.md#status) bit until it becomes 1.
requirements.note: After the absorbing step; line 35 says the kmac_done interrupt is raised at the same point.

requirements.text: The software should check [`STATUS.squeeze`](registers.md#status) register field for the readiness of [`STATE`](registers.md#state) value.

design.description: the CMD register (lines 622 to 771) has no field named mode; its fields are cmd, entropy_req, hash_cnt_clr and err_processed

design.note: CFG_SHADOWED.mode selects SHA3, SHAKE or cSHAKE.
The hand-written top level takes the mode from CFG_SHADOWED.

design.description: the STATUS register (lines 772 to 875) has no field named squeeze

design.note: STATUS.sha3_squeeze: "If 1, SHA3 completes sponge absorbing stage. In this stage, SW can manually run the hashing engine."

claims.setting: CMD has a field named mode (1 yes, 0 no)
claims.label: disagrees

claims.setting: CFG_SHADOWED has a field named mode that sets the hashing mode (1 yes, 0 no)
claims.label: agrees

claims.setting: STATUS has a field named squeeze (1 yes, 0 no)
claims.label: disagrees

claims.setting: STATUS has a bit that is 1 once absorbing is complete (1 yes, 0 no)
claims.label: agrees

generated_from_same_input: D1, D2, D4 and D5 are in kmac.hjson, from which reggen generates the register RTL and registers.md; those generated files are not counted as further evidence. D3 and D6 are in the hand-written kmac.sv. R1 to R5 are hand-written.
finding: The programmer's guide (R2) and another passage of the theory of operation (R3) put the mode in CFG_SHADOWED.mode, which is where the design reads it (D2, D3). R1, in the theory of operation's section on KMAC padding, gives the same instruction with CMD.mode; CMD has no mode field (D1), only the command and error-handling fields. Separately, R4 and R5 name the squeeze status bit STATUS.squeeze; the bit exists and behaves as described (C4), but its name is sha3_squeeze (C3).
missing_information: This case reads the register description and the top-level assignments; it does not simulate an operation.
ambiguities: STATUS.squeeze is close enough to STATUS.sha3_squeeze that a reader is likely to find the right bit; CMD.mode points to a different register, where a reader would not find it.
out_of_scope: The PREFIX value in R1, which is not compared here.
CFG_SHADOWED is a shadowed register and must be written twice; the documents state this elsewhere.
